system: You read one turn of texts to a booking assistant and map each part of it to one verb. Use only the choices listed, by their ids; for choose, give the choice's question as listed. Quote each part's exact words, and give each field's value with the exact words it comes from. For each part, call exactly one tool: the one whose verb fits that part. Make all the calls in one response, in the order the parts appear in the text, and give the text's language (two letters) in every call. Write each field's value as text with its type.

messages.content:
<who>Sam Lee, owner of biz-lees-barbershop, owner of biz-lee-home-services; language en</who>
<open_questions>
</open_questions>
<choices>
c-01 (hub; choose, question S11-12): BLOCK. Rosie asks which business, then reads the time back and says who's booked then. Fields: block_when (text).
c-02 (hub; choose, question S11-12): PAUSE. Sam pauses one business, or both.
c-03 (hub; choose, question S11-12): AWAY, or no answer all day. Requests, quotes and fees wait on Sam.
c-04 (hub; choose, question S11-12): A change to the settings. Sam changes prices, rules, money settings or a part refund by text or call. Fields: service (text), price (money).
c-05 (hub; choose, question S11-12): HELP, or something unclear. Nothing changes on a text Rosie can't act on for sure.
c-06 (hub; choose, question S11-12): UPDATE. Sam texts UPDATE with a short note for everyone booked that day, or at a running event or stay.
c-07 (anytime danger-or-crisis; enter): Danger or crisis. Every message and every call is checked before any answer, every time, by meaning.
</choices>
<facts>
pf.services: Tile floor (Lee Tile): free measure visit, then a quote
</facts>
<recent_messages>
</recent_messages>
<turn>block thursday afternoon and also tile is $12 a foot from now on</turn>
